course_description:
This course will cover the principles of quantum technologies, how to apply them to understand the results of experiments, and how to use them to design robust quantum devices. It will cover the topics of high precision sensing, quantum information, quantum communication and computation, noise and error suppression, and quantum error correction.

This course covers quantum information and algorithms, quantum noise and errors, and physical architectures for quantum technology.ﾠ

In the School of Mathematics and Physics we are committed to creating an inclusive and empowering learning environment for all students. We value and respect the diverse range of experiences our students bring to their education, and we believe that this diversity is crucial for fostering a rich culture of knowledge sharing and meaningful exploration. We hold both students and staff accountable for actively contributing to the establishment of a respectful and supportive learning environment.

Bullying, harassment, and discrimination in any form are strictly against our principles and against ﾠ UQ Policy, ﾠ and will not be tolerated. We have developed a ﾠ suite of resources ﾠto assist you in recognising, reporting, and addressing such behaviour. If you have any concerns about your experience in this course, we encourage you to tell a member of the course teaching team, or alternatively contact an SMP Classroom Inclusivity Champion (see Blackboard for contact details). Our Inclusivity Champions are here to listen, to understand your concerns, and to explore potential actions that can be taken to resolve them. Your well-being and a positive learning atmosphere are of utmost importance to us.

learning_outcomes.description: Use the formalism of quantum information to describe quantum circuits and algorithms
Apply methods from quantum noise to describe simple noise processes.
Describe the methods of quantum error correction theory and apply them to correct quantum errors.
Determine the requirements of physical systems to be good for implementations of quantum information and give quantitative calculations analysing various physical platforms.
Describe and understand the quantum information "stack" from physical hardware to algorithms.

assessment_details.task_description: For a subset of the applied class sections throughout the semester a subset of students will be selected to complete a “viva” style question, to be worked through individually and presented individually (no external resources allowed beyond the course notes and textbook).The class will be divided into groups of typically 3 depending on numbers. Each group will present once during the semester during the applied class time. The assessment will proceed as follows: - The selected group of students will attend the applied class and be presented the question(s), and will be given 20 min. to individually prepare notes on a response to one of the questions. - The students will then take turns presenting their solution over the next 30 minutes (~10 minutes each) with interactive questions from the lecturer. This assessment item will be audio-visually recorded and retained in accordance with University requirements. Read full task description Hide full task description
